claims.text: Human-AI teams can outperform individual humans working alone.
Human-AI teams often do not exceed the performance of AI working alone.
Larger LLMs perform on par with or surpass humans in certain Theory of Mind task conditions.
Users increase their trust in LLM responses when explanations are present, even if those responses are deceptive.

evidence.description: Prior empirical studies demonstrate that human-AI teams achieve higher accuracy than individual humans.
Evaluations across collaborative benchmarks show human-AI team performance frequently fails to surpass standalone AI performance.
Evaluations comparing GPT-4 and children/adults on advanced Theory of Mind tests showed GPT-4 meeting or exceeding human performance levels.
User trust studies report increased participant reliance when LLM responses include explanatory rationales, even in misleading scenarios.

limitations.text: The article is a perspective synthesis and does not conduct new empirical experiments or formal benchmark evaluations of the proposed interaction paradigms.
Existing Large Language Models suffer from hallucinations, prompt sensitivity, and sycophantic alignment.
Current learning-to-defer methods rely on a binary separation of responsibility, leaving humans unassisted when AI defers.

future_work.text: Develop cognitive-science-inspired metrics to evaluate human-LLM team interaction and reasoning quality.
Adapt complementary team performance strategies to general-purpose, arbitrary user interaction contexts.
Implement and empirically test confrontational or antagonistic AI strategies to mitigate human confirmation bias.
